_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint or onboard --resume must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and FAILS CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: manifest.json name/entry_point/command use the clean `veeam-mcp`, not the press `-pp-mcp`
handfixes.why: onboard.py re-copies the SOURCE manifest.json on every --resume, and the printing-press source keeps the `-pp-mcp` convention. The repo builds/ships `veeam-mcp`, so a stale `-pp-mcp` name mismatches the .mcpb the release matrix produces. See project_onboard_manifest_deleak_and_envvar.

handfixes.summary: VEEAM_BASE_URL is a required env var in manifest.json + server.json (per-instance appliance URL)
handfixes.why: VSPC is appliance-hosted, so the REST base URL is per-instance; config.go reads VEEAM_BASE_URL and the placeholder default (your-vspc-host:1280) is dead. The press generated the manifest with only VEEAM_TOKEN (the per-instance BASE_URL-omission pattern), so a fresh reprint drops it again. server.json also marks BASE_URL non-secret (it is a URL). See project_onboard_perinstance_baseurl_and_bareword_claims.

handfixes.summary: Governance gates the large VSPC write surface: an 'Infrastructure and agent execution' tier, a Destructive tier, and secret-returning reads placed in Credential (not Read)
handfixes.why: VSPC has ~410 write/destructive commands. gen_governance is method-blind: it lumped install-backup-agent-on-computer / reboot-computer / start-rule / force-collect (run software on real customer machines) into 'Write (routine)' and produced no infra tier. The get-*-credentials-by-server / get-*-encryption-passwords-by-server commands RETURN stored secrets and must be Credential, not Read, even though the binary tags them mcp:read-only. A full reprint re-runs the classifier and reverts. See feedback_secret_read_commands_not_read_tier + project_action1_onboard_traps.

handfixes.summary: page.json command examples use the stripped `veeam-cli`, never the source `veeam-pp-cli`
handfixes.why: The generated SKILL.md/source examples use `veeam-pp-cli`; the INSTALLED binary is `veeam-cli`. page.json command examples authored from the source leaked `veeam-pp-cli`, which propagated into the published docs page + llms corpus (copy-paste fails: that name is not on PATH). check_cli_claims is BLIND to the binary-name prefix, so only adversarial review caught it. A reprint/re-author must keep the stripped name. See feedback_outcome_prose_must_match_command_output_fields.

handfixes.summary: SKILL.md + guide.md stay free of Printing Press / npx-library / go-install / openclaw-install-block leaks
handfixes.why: onboard.py only de-leaks the SKILL.md description, not the body H1/prereqs/HeyGen-Beacon/MCP-install lines, the openclaw frontmatter `install:` block (a printing-press-library go module path), or guide.md's npx/go install section. A reprint re-vendors both and re-introduces the leaks. See project_onboard_skillmd_guide_deleak.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. veeam was already correct on all three channels; the ledger entry exists so a re-onboard cannot make it wrong. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 3 commands listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs them
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: infrastructure abort-backup-server-multipart-patch (POST /infrastructure/backupServers/{backupServerUid}/patch/upload/multipart/abort); licensing finalize-reports (POST /licensing/reports/finalization); plugins enabled enable-disable-plugin (POST /plugins/{pluginId}/enabled).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: The seven local-mirror reports name the documented VSPC list path and resolve it to the sync partition through the generated syncResourcePath, failing when no partition fetches it
handfixes.why: Press 4.35.1 renamed sync partitions ("alarms" now syncs /alarms/templates, active alarms are "alarms-active", agent jobs are "infrastructure"), so a report that read partition names would have reported alarm templates as active alarms. veeamLoad(ctx, db, paths...) resolves each documented path via veeamSyncNames, fails when nothing fetches it, propagates store read errors and de-duplicates on instanceUid. Hand files: a reprint that restores the published 0.1.7 novels brings the defect back. TestNovelPathsResolveToSyncPartitions fails on a renamed partition.

handfixes.summary: The reports read the documented VSPC shapes: tenant is mappedOrganizationUid for server jobs, only Active agents are online, job health maps the documented enums (WaitingRepository included), license points sum servers[].workloads[].usedUnits where unitType is Points, Resolved alarms are not active, alarms group on tenant/template/object UIDs
handfixes.why: The published 0.1.7 novels counted per-OS agent lists twice, read NotRunning as online, read an undocumented top-level usedPoints (always 0), attributed jobs to the server owner, counted Resolved alarms, claimed a first_seen no synced field supports, and merged distinct alarm objects that share a display name. Print review rounds 1 and 2 (failing-first tests in veeam_review_r1_test.go and veeam_review_r2_test.go).

handfixes.summary: The reports refuse a missing mirror and any partition with no sync record or an unfinished last sync, instead of reporting a partial mirror as the whole fleet
handfixes.why: A partial mirror reported as a whole one reads as a healthy fleet. veeamOpenStoreRead errors on a missing mirror; veeamLoad refuses a partition with no sync_state row or last_attempt_complete != 1. Consequence: press verify (mock, never syncs) scores the novels' EXEC leg FAIL by design. TestNovelsRefuseAnIncompleteMirror.

handfixes.summary: SKILL.md and guide.md describe VEEAM_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 as the binary behaves: only tools marked read-only stay; the execute tool, sync, import, export and the learn-store writers are removed
handfixes.why: The press 4.35.1 SKILL.md/guide.md text says local-write learn-store tools stay and the raw execute tool refuses state-changing calls, but tools/list under VEEAM_MCP_READ_ONLY=1 lists 21 tools with no veeam_execute, sync, import, export, teach, learnings_confirm or workflow_archive (34 without it). Both files are re-vendored on every onboard --resume.

handfixes.summary: The seven local-mirror reports count only the records the last finished, unrestricted sync walk of each partition returned (store table veeam_walk), so a narrowed walk, a walk capped by --max-pages and not resumed, a live read's write-through, an import, or a record the API has since deleted is never reported as part of the fleet
handfixes.why: sync_state.last_attempt_complete=1 proves only that the requested walk ended, not that it covered the collection: `sync --resources infrastructure-backup-servers-jobs --param offset=1` over jobs ordered Failed, Success stored only the Success job and finished, and fleet-health reported one success and zero failures (Codex, review class incomplete-read-coverage). The generated sync.go carries three hooks: veeamWalkBegin after the attempt-start checkpoint, seenIDs collection for walk-tracked partitions, and veeamWalkEnd after the final sync-state save (skipped on dry run). veeam_walk.go keeps per-partition membership: carried across a --max-pages resume, never touched by a --param, --resource-param, --global-param or since walk, broken by an out-of-order resume or a stored row it could not key. veeamLoad (veeam_fleet.go) reads only members and refuses an unproven partition, naming the `veeam-cli sync --resources <name>` (or `--full`) run that fixes it; store/veeam_walk.go writes the record under the store write lock. A reprint that drops the sync.go hooks fails closed (no walk is ever recorded, so every report refuses), not open. Tests drive the real sync command against a loopback VSPC fake that answers with the documented paging envelope.

handfixes.summary: The generated pp:happy-args annotation on infrastructure delete-backup-server-encryption-password uses low-entropy placeholder UIDs, so gitleaks does not read passwordUid=<uuid> as a leaked password
handfixes.why: Press 4.35.1 emits pp:happy-args from the spec's path examples (spec repair 1 gave every path parameter the RFC 4122 sample UUID 3f2504e0-4f89-11d3-9a0c-0305e82c3301). gitleaks' generic-api-key rule matches `passwordUid=<high-entropy value>` and verify_all/CI fail. The UIDs are not secrets; a low-entropy placeholder keeps the example runnable. Spec-side follow-up: prep.py could give passwordUid a low-entropy example so a reprint emits this by construction.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand: internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one credkit.Declarations literal, both mains start with credkit.Start(credwire.Declarations) and end with credkit.Exit, every HTTP client (API, --deliver webhook and Spacefast, feedback, probe) goes through credkit.Transport, every SQLite handle through the credkit.SQLDriver internal/credsql registers, every program file write through the kit, child processes through credkit.RunCommand, and the MCP stdio and HTTP servers through credkit.MCPTools, MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPHTTP. The credential store, config and the Spacefast delivery record are sources, written outside the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile). VSPC response fields that carry a third-party credential (stored Linux keys and passphrases, generated RSA keys and TOTP secrets, new API key logins and the rest, by wire name) are declared ResponseFields, so they are held as they arrive, except password, rootPassword and sshPrivateKey: VSPC answers those with a masked placeholder (a run of U+2022, *, U+FFFD), which the kit would hold, so cliutil.HoldMaskedResponseFields holds every value under them but a mask (cliutil.IsCredentialMask) at the one point every API response body passes after the kit transport and before any sink (client doInternal, its XML conversion, and the Spacefast deliver client), and withholds a body it cannot read as JSON that names one of them; cliutil.HoldMaskedResponseHeaders does the same for the final response's headers and trailers and, from CheckRedirect (redirectGuard), for every redirect response.
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector's own layer: secret-echo-decoded-funnel is retired, replaced by the shared credential kit (the press 4.35.1 reprint dropped its files; not a `retired` record because check_handfixes.py accepts only registry-backed retirements and fleet_handfixes.json delegates that id to apply_secret_funnel.py). Classes closed, each by a built-binary test seen failing first on the pre-kit build (.review/seen/kit-fail.log): an API error that echoes VEEAM_TOKEN, a piece of it, base64 or URL-encoded (TestAPIErrorEchoOfTokenIsWithheld, CLI, --agent and MCP); credential response fields reaching stdout, the MCP result and the response cache (TestResponseCredentialFieldsWithheld) and the SQLite store on sync (TestSyncNeverStoresACredentialField); an unconfirmed MCP veeam_execute preview that echoed the password param (TestMCPExecutePreviewWithholdsPassword); --password, --private-key, --passphrase and --api-key held before the flag parser, and the credential fields inside a JSON-valued flag such as --credentials held one by one (credwire.HoldJSONArguments, right after Start), so no --dry-run preview prints them (TestCLICredentialFlagsHeld); a profile value under a credential flag held at startup (TestProfileCredentialValueHeldAtStartup); a held credential refused to another origin and over plain http (TestHeldCredentialRefusedOffOriginAndOverPlainHTTP); SPACEFAST_TOKEN and VEEAM_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN held (TestSinkTokensHeld); the learn journal and the feedback ledger never record a held credential (TestJournalNeverRecordsAHeldCredential, TestFeedbackStdinIsRecorded). A malformed config's token stays held at startup (TestMalformedConfigCredentialHeldAtStartup, a guard: the press already passed it). In-process tests never run Start, so cliutil.OutboundGuard, Hold and HoldBody are variables the seams swap (credkit_seam_test.go in cli, mcp, client). The MCP sql value cap moved from sqlite.Limit on a held connection to the _length_limit DSN parameter, and the read-only store runs select 1 because the kit's connection does not forward Ping. The three masked names were held in connector code once a built-binary test showed the declared mask breaking ordinary use (.review/seen/mask-fail.log): with VSPC's documented "password": "••••••" a plain sync exited non-zero, the agent-jobs partition was withheld through a kit matcher false positive and fleet-health refused, and every backup policy, discovery rule and guest OS credential read printed the withhold notice (TestMaskedPasswordPlaceholderIsNotHeld). A real value under those names (GET /infrastructure/managementAgents/{uid}/credentials, a duplicate or escaped key, a number, a nested value, a body that is not JSON, a refused redirect's Location query, a response header pair) is still held before any sink (TestRealValueUnderMaskedFieldNamesHeld, revert-proven by removing the body hold, the non-JSON withhold and the header hold in turn); the mask function is unit-tested (TestIsCredentialMask, TestHoldMaskedResponseFieldsJSON, TestHoldMaskedResponseFieldsNotJSON, TestHoldMaskedResponseHeaders).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring, the Declarations literal and one kit-wrapped SQLite driver name.

handfixes.summary: README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json say the ChatGPT desktop app runs this connector locally (STDIO) and that ChatGPT on the web, Microsoft 365 Copilot / Copilot Studio and the Gemini app are not supported by msp-skills yet, with a link to the hosted-gateway comparison; no paid-plan list, no Developer Mode recipe, no 'ChatGPT connects only to remote servers'.
handfixes.why: Docs fix approved 2026-11-03, following PR #502. OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py, whose template still writes the old ChatGPT text, so without this entry a re-onboard or reprint silently restores it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Change the ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Gemini app text in onboard.py (cc-skills msp-skills-publish) so a regeneration writes this wording itself, then this entry can be retired.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

retired.reason: tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0 builds a per-command blocked set (blockedDestinationFlags, blockedInputFlags, root control-plane flags), removes those flags from each tool's schema, refuses any undeclared argument name (so "db=/path" is refused) and skips '=' names in cliArgsFromMCP.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #4647: every value-carrying branch of cliArgsFromMCP joins the value to its flag (--k=v, one element per list item), and the press generates TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
